changes.comment: Settle resident turns by attributing each `result` envelope to the command it answers (`result.user_message_uuid`) instead of gating on `command_lifecycle` terminal state, and parse `command_lifecycle` as a top-level `type` (the resident CLI's actual wire shape, keeping the `system`-subtype shape for backward compatibility). The previous lifecycle gate never opened for top-level envelopes, so turns hung until the 600s idle reap even though `result` had arrived. A steered turn spans several commands and the CLI answers each with its own `result`, seconds apart in separate stdout flushes: the turn now settles only once every submitted command has produced a result and takes the last submission's outcome, matching the Codex runtime's active-turn slot, so a steered send no longer returns the pre-steer answer. A `result` whose `user_message_uuid` was not submitted by the pending turn is warned about and dropped instead of settling it with another turn's answer; a result carrying no `user_message_uuid` (older builds) still settles the turn; a command reported `cancelled`/`discarded` leaves the turn's waited-on set with a warning instead of hanging it, and does not fail a turn whose other commands can still settle it. When a turn loses every one of its commands that way (cancelled, discarded, or a failed steer write) nothing can answer it, so it now fails immediately with the last drop's cause instead of waiting for the idle deadline, which would have reaped a healthy resident child. A `result` arriving with no pending turn logs a warning instead of being dropped silently.
